opportunities.title: Historic buildings and structures (Preservation and Conservation grants)

amount.raw: Generally, £1,000 to £30,000 (average approx. £15,000). Sometimes larger sums are considered.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK registered charity, organisation with exempt charitable status, recognised public body, Community Benefit Society, or Community Interest Company (CIC) limited by guarantee. Project must be UK based, not complete, and focus on a listed building or structure.
opportunities.summary: Funds the preservation, conservation and repair of listed historic buildings, structures and architectural features, with special consideration for those at risk, of outstanding importance, or finding sustainable re-use. Covers project costs, staff costs, fees, internships, initial exploratory work and capital costs. Applications accepted at any time on a rolling basis; stage-two applications above £5,000 considered quarterly at Board meetings.

opportunities.title: Places of worship (Preservation and Conservation grants)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK registered charity, organisation with exempt charitable status, or recognised public body. Anglican churches must apply via the ChurchCare conservation grants scheme; other denominations, faiths and cathedrals apply directly to the Trust. Project must be UK based and not complete.
opportunities.summary: Funds the conservation of historic interiors and historic objects in listed places of worship open for regular worship, including bells, books and manuscripts, clocks, decorative plasterwork, metalwork and church plate, monuments, organs, paintings, stained glass, textiles, timberwork, wall paintings and historic structures in churchyards, plus commissioning of conservation reports. Applications accepted at any time on a rolling basis; stage-two applications above £5,000 considered quarterly at Board meetings.

opportunities.title: Conservation of cultural heritage (Preservation and Conservation grants)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK registered charity, organisation with exempt charitable status, recognised public body, Community Benefit Society, or Community Interest Company (CIC) limited by guarantee. Applicants must not be eligible for the AIM and NMCT grant schemes. Project must be UK based and not complete.
opportunities.summary: Funds the conservation of culturally and historically significant collections and objects, including works of art, books, significant ephemera, artefacts and archives. Supports project costs including staff costs, fees, paid internships, initial exploratory work and conservation costs carried out by accredited conservators, and encourages knowledge sharing and public access. Applications accepted at any time on a rolling basis; stage-two applications above £5,000 considered quarterly at Board meetings.

opportunities.title: Archives Revealed
opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK registered charity, organisation with exempt charitable status, or recognised public body. Project must be UK based and not complete.
opportunities.summary: A partnership funding programme between The National Archives, The National Lottery Heritage Fund, the Pilgrim Trust and the Wolfson Foundation - the only UK grant programme dedicated to cataloguing and unlocking archival collections, ensuring significant archive collections are made accessible to the public. Applications are made via the National Archives website.

opportunities.title: Research, advocacy and development fund
opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK registered charity, organisation with exempt charitable status, recognised public body, Community Benefit Society, or Community Interest Company (CIC) limited by guarantee. Supports projects/organisations doing research, advocacy and sector development in young women's mental health and preservation and conservation.
opportunities.summary: A small-pot fund for strategic interventions in the Trust's areas of interest (young women's mental health and preservation and conservation of historic buildings and collections) that may bring about systemic change, drive forward policy and practice, or strengthen the sector. The approach is conversational/invitation-based; the Trust is currently unlikely to support further research and advocacy work in young women's mental health as proposals are already under development.
